source.label: The Duelist Sideboard #5 (Feb 1997), 'A Day at the Classic Zoo', top 2 decklists, p. 9

notes.text: Placings, seeds (place after seven Swiss rounds) and the 95-player standings from Wizards' Pro Tour-Dallas Day 1 results page. Quarterfinals: Johns def. Guevin 2-1, Fleischman def. Kuta 2-1, Shwe def. Ferker 2-0, O'Mahoney-Schwartz def. Cargilo 2-0; semifinals Johns def. O'Mahoney-Schwartz 2-1, Shwe def. Fleischman 2-0; final Johns def. Shwe 2-1.
Played Friday 22 November 1996, before the Pro Tour's Standard event; $40,000 purse. The Wizards results page and Sideboard #5 agree on all eight names and finishes.

Sideboard #5 prints only the top two lists. Fleischman and O'Mahoney-Schwartz played the same deck, described but not listed (18 lands, five colorless; all five Moxen, Sol Ring, Black Lotus; Serendib Efreets and Erhnam Djinns; four Birds of Paradise in the sideboard). The Dojo's 'NY Zoo, Nov '96 - Jul '97' (which MTG Wiki gives as O'Mahoney-Schwartz's Dallas list) is a Neutral Ground group deck with Patrick Johnson's comments, not identified as the Dallas list, and has 19 lands and three Birds; it is not used.

Sideboard #5 prints 2 Kird Ape and 2 Savannah, a 58-card main deck (checked against the page scan). The Dojo's list of the same deck has 4 Kird Ape and 4 Savannah (62 cards). Kird Ape is corrected to 4 from the Dojo, giving 60; Savannah is left at 2 as Sideboard #5 printed it. Which count was wrong cannot be settled from these two sources; MTG Wiki has the same 60.
Sideboard #5 says he 'dubbed it the "Turbo/Zoo"'; its report calls the deck 'The Zoo', as does the Dojo.
Main deck is 65 cards as printed (checked against the page scan; legal, Type I had no maximum). No second source.
Shared deck with O'Mahoney-Schwartz; described in Sideboard #5 but not listed.
Shared deck with Fleischman; described in Sideboard #5 but not listed. See the event note on the Dojo 'NY Zoo'.
'Thomas Guevin' on the Day 1 page and in Sideboard #5's standings; 'Tom Guevin' on the results page.
